text.p: Simeon Wines Ltd said on Friday it would provide an alternative takeover offer for Australian Vintage Ltd, which would give AustVin shareholders a higher cash component for their shares.

AustVin directors had said they would unanimously recommend that shareholders accept the revised offer, incorporating the alternative, in the absence of any more favourable offer, Simeon said in a statement.
Simeon launched its takeover offer on April 22, offering four Simon shares plus A$3.60 cash for every five AustVin shares.
This offer would remain in place, and an alternative would offer one Simeon share plus A$3.16 cash for every two AustVin shares.
Simeon said this meant for every 10 AustVin shares, shareholders could accept either eight Simeon shares plus A$7.20 cash, or five Simeon shares plus A$15.80 cash.
Shareholders who had accepted the original offer could elect to switch.

"We are pleased to have an unanimous recommendations from AustVin directors that AustVin shareholders accept the offer which now includes an alternative with a higher cash component," siad AustVin chairman John Branson.
Simeon said it would potentially need an extra A$32 million cash to fund the alternative offer.
The funds would be raised through a share placement underwritten by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Australia Ltd, for the issue of up to about 10.6 million new shares at A$3.05 a share.
The number of shares issued would depend on the amount needed to fund the alternative offer.
Simeon shares closed up two cents at A$3.22 on Friday, while AustVin ended steady at A$3.20.
Simeon has said previously a successful merger would create Australia's fourth largest winemaker by volume.
Assets of a merged group would include:
- two wine processing facilities with capacity of 100,000 tonnes processing 12 percent of Australia's wine grape crop with access to fruit from Australia's largest grape growing regions.
- 3,000 acres of vineyards in the Padthaway, Cowra, Riverland and Sunraysia districts.
